assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear invention with decisive, lasting impact: correcting spherical aberration in electron lenses overcame a limit recognised since Scherzer and delivered routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of interfaces, defects, oxides and nanoparticles across materials physics, chemistry and engineering. From the standpoint of working electron microscopy, it changed what can be measured and is a concrete invention rather than lifetime achievement.
assessment.attribution: The credited trio maps well onto the history as I know it: Rose's theoretical aberration-corrector design, Haider's realisation of the hexapole corrector in the TEM, and Urban's demonstration with Haider that it yields atomic-resolution gains in materials. The credited list does not include other people sometimes named in this area (for example Krivanek and collaborators on the STEM corrector), so a three-person prize would implicitly settle a TEM-versus-STEM credit question that I cannot resolve from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than two decades of independent confirmation, commercial instruments worldwide, and the technique is now routine. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether credit for STEM aberration correction (not among the credited names) should be recognised alongside the TEM work.
Precise priority and division of credit between theoretical design and the first working correctors rests on my own recollection, not independent verification here.
Possible perception that this is an instrumentation prize in a field the committee has recognised before (electron microscopy 1986); I do not consider that disqualifying.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new paradigm in condensed matter physics: the quantum spin Hall state, Z2 topological classification and protected edge and surface states, with wide reach into materials, spintronics and quantum devices. The idea is original and the physics is clear.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical prediction and Z2 classification; Molenkamp led the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe wells. The supplied names fit a theory-plus-experiment configuration. Other contributors to the HgTe prediction and to 3D topological insulators exist and are not in the credited list, so completeness of credit is a real question.
assessment.maturity: Mature: roughly two decades of independent confirmation across HgTe, Bi-based materials and ARPES and transport measurements, though it overlaps conceptually with the 2016 topological-phase prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions and whether the committee sees this as a distinct discovery.
Credit for the HgTe quantum-well proposal and for three-dimensional topological insulators beyond the named people.
The ranking among the two related topological candidates on the list (B019 and B039) is a judgement about which framing is cleaner.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock achieves fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, redefining precision metrology and enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and prospective redefinition of the second. The magic-wavelength lattice idea is original and elegant.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and demonstrated early realisations; Ye developed the leading strontium clocks and pushed them to record accuracy and coherence. Two laureates is a clean configuration. Others contributed to related ion and lattice clocks, so the boundary of the discovery needs care.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the scientific sense: multiple independent labs reproduce and exceed the performance. The redefinition of the second has not yet occurred, but the scientific case is secure.
uncertainties: Relation to the 2005 prize for laser-based precision spectroscopy and frequency combs, and to ion-clock work.
Whether other groups' contributions to lattice clocks should be part of the credit.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for the redefinition of the second.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution is a conceptually original application of quantum mechanics to information security, with BB84 and the entanglement-based E91 protocol linking foundations and technology. It has produced working networks and satellite links and complements the 2022 recognition of entanglement experiments.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84; Ekert proposed the entanglement-based protocol. The three credited names form a natural configuration. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not in the list and bears on priority; I cannot resolve this from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Mature in concept and increasingly in practice, although practical security and deployment remain debated. Fundamental impact is clearly established.
uncertainties: Priority questions around earlier conjugate-coding ideas not credited here.
Practical security of real implementations versus idealised protocols.
Ballot B014 describes a related candidate with teleportation; I treat B059 as the cleaner discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Twisted bilayer graphene created a tunable platform for correlated insulators, superconductivity and related phases, and it launched twistronics. The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction and the experimental demonstration make a clear theory-to-experiment story. Electron microscopy and spectroscopy played a role in characterising twist angle and relaxation.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero led the experimental discovery of correlated and superconducting phases. The first author of the key experimental papers (not in the credited list) is a notable omission in a strict three-person limit, and a fair configuration may be disputed.
assessment.maturity: Relatively recent, since 2018, but replicated broadly. The microscopic mechanism of superconductivity and some correlated phases is still debated, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The origin of the correlated phases is not settled.
Credit for early experimental work and for the idea of a twist-angle-controlled flat band beyond the three named.
Timing: the field is still evolving rapidly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides strong light-matter coupling on a chip and is the architecture of most superconducting quantum processors, enabling dispersive readout and gates. The idea is original, clear and technologically transformative.
assessment.attribution: Blais proposed the circuit QED architecture with collaborators, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf realised it experimentally with Yale colleagues. The credited names map to a theory-plus-two-experiment configuration, which strains the three-person limit and leaves out other Yale contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature in scientific confirmation and widely adopted. Close in time and subject to the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, so the committee may judge it too soon.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize and whether the committee prefers to wait.
Credit among Yale team members and the relation to earlier cavity QED work.
Whether the discovery is separable from quantum-computing engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imaging a black-hole shadow at horizon scale is a landmark achievement combining very long baseline interferometry, calibration and imaging algorithms. It directly tests strong-field gravity and has clear public and scientific impact.
assessment.attribution: The result came from a collaboration of hundreds, and the Event Horizon Telescope leaders, the proposers of the shadow measurement and the developers of imaging methods are different people. The three credited names represent leadership and concept but a three-person limit makes fair credit difficult.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by two sources (M87* and Sgr A*) and repeated epochs, but interpretation, spin and jet constraints are still being refined.
uncertainties: Collaborative credit cannot be mapped cleanly to three people.
Black-hole physics was recognised in 2020, so the committee may see overlap.
Remaining dependence on modelling for physical interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new window onto supermassive black-hole binaries or early-universe physics and rests on decades of precision pulsar timing.
assessment.attribution: The evidence emerged from several regional collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA and others) and long-term pulsar timing infrastructure, so decisive credit is spread. The listed names represent leaders of different efforts. Any three will leave out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Premature: the 2023 evidence is at a few sigma, the expected angular correlation is not yet firmly established and the source is not identified.
uncertainties: Statistical significance and source of the signal are still under study.
Credit allocation across collaborations is unresolved.
Whether a prize before confirmation at discovery-level significance would be timely.
